## 4\. Strengthening the construction to polynomial numerical coefficient heights

There is one additional resource issue worth eliminating. The cosine-power construction (1) has polynomial *binary* coefficient lengths, but its Fourier denominators can be exponentially large as integers.

To satisfy even the stricter interpretation that the numerators and denominators themselves must be polynomially bounded in \(R\), use the following modification. **This is the final algorithm for the full resource contract.**

Keep

\[
A_0=R^{100},\qquad n=R^{200},
\]

but set

\[
M=R^6,\qquad N=2M+1
\]

and define the normalized Dirichlet polynomial

\[
D_M(\theta)=
\frac{1+2\sum_{j=1}^{M}\cos(2\pi j\theta)}{2M+1}.
\]

Define the nonnegative localization kernel

\[
J_M(\theta)=D_M(\theta)^{32}.
\]

Replace every \(P_m\) in Section 1 by \(J_M\), obtaining

\[
\begin{aligned}
v_1&=J_M(y)\big[J_M(z)-J_M(z-\tfrac12)\big],\\
v_2&=\big[J_M(x)-J_M(x-\tfrac12)\big]J_M(z-\tfrac14),\\
v_3&=\big[J_M(x-\tfrac14)-J_M(x-\tfrac34)\big]J_M(y-\tfrac14).
\end{aligned}
\tag{4}
\]

The final controller is

\[
\boxed{b(x)=nA_0v(nx).}
\tag{5}
\]

This has the same channel geometry but better exact coefficient bounds.

### Exact arithmetic properties

Because

\[
D_M(\theta)=\frac1N\sum_{j=-M}^{M}e^{2\pi ij\theta},
\]

the coefficients of \(J_M\) have denominator \(N^{32}\) and integer numerators bounded by \(N^{32}\)\.

Each component of \(v\) is a sum of at most two products of such kernels. Consequently, after multiplication by \(nA_0\), the absolute numerator and denominator of every Fourier coefficient are bounded by

\[
10nA_0N^{64}
\leq 10\cdot3^{64}R^{684}.
\]

In particular, **even the unlogged rational coefficient height is polynomial in \(R\)**\.

Also,

\[
0\leq J_M\leq1,\qquad
\deg J_M\leq32M.
\]

The shifts by quarters preserve rational trigonometric coefficients.

---

## 6\. A quantitative Bloch-mode hypocoercivity lemma

We now prove the estimate that converts this geometry into rapid scalar dissipation.

Consider the periodic complex-valued operator

\[
\mathcal L_\eta
=\kappa(\nabla+i\eta)^2
-A_0v\cdot(\nabla+i\eta),
\]

where \(\eta\in\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}\), and suppose

\[

\beta:=A_0|\eta|\leq\kappa,\qquad
A_0\,10^{12}M^{-30}\leq\kappa.
\tag{8}
\]

**Quantitative lemma.** Under (6)–(8),

\[
\boxed{
\|e^{\tau\mathcal L_\eta}\|_{L^2\to L^2}
\leq
2\exp\left(
-\frac{\beta^2\tau}
{4\cdot10^{60}\kappa M^8}
\right)
\quad(\tau\geq0).
}
\tag{9}
\]

The norm includes arbitrary periodic complex initial functions, including their constant Fourier component.

## 7\. Every Fourier block contracts by \(\epsilon\)

We now apply the lemma to the physical controller (5).

Because \(v(nx)\) has only Fourier frequencies divisible by \(n\), the physical operator preserves the orthogonal Fourier residue subspaces

\[
\mathcal H_q=
\overline{\operatorname{span}}
\left\{
e^{2\pi i(q+n\ell)\cdot x}:
\ell\in\mathbb Z^3
\right\},
\]

where each component of \(q\) is chosen in a centred residue interval modulo \(n\)\.

We distinguish three cases.

### Case A: \(q=0\)

After removing the global constant, every Fourier frequency in this subspace has length at least \(n\)\.

The ordinary diffusion energy identity therefore gives

\[
\|S_i(t)|_{\mathcal H_0\cap L^2_0}\|
\leq e^{-4\pi^2\kappa_i n^2t}
\leq\epsilon.
\tag{14}
\]

No enhancement estimate is needed.

### Case B: \(|q|>R^2\)

Every Fourier frequency in \(\mathcal H_q\) has length at least \(|q|\)\. Since advection is skew-adjoint,

\[
\|S_i(t)|_{\mathcal H_q}\|
\leq e^{-4\pi^2\kappa_i|q|^2t}.
\]

Using \(\kappa_i t\geq R^{-2}\),

\[
\boxed{
\|S_i(t)|_{\mathcal H_q}\|
\leq e^{-4\pi^2R^2}
\leq\epsilon.
}
\tag{15}
\]

### Case C: \(0<|q|\leq R^2\)

Write a function in this block as

\[
f(x)=e^{2\pi iq\cdot x}g(nx).
\]

Under this substitution, the physical generator becomes

\[
n^2\mathcal L_\eta,
\qquad
\eta=\frac{2\pi q}{n}.
\]

Since \(n=R^{200}\),

\[
|\eta|
\leq7R^{-198}<1.
\]

Also,

\[
\beta=A_0|\eta|
\leq7R^{-98}
\leq R^{-1}\leq\kappa_i.
\]

The self-advection condition follows from (6)\:

\[
\frac{A_0\,10^{12}M^{-30}}{\kappa_i}
\leq10^{12}R^{101-180}
=10^{12}R^{-79}<1.
\]

All hypotheses of the quantitative lemma hold for every \(\kappa_i\)\.

Applying (9) at microscopic time \(\tau=n^2t\),

\[
\begin{aligned}
\|S_i(t)|_{\mathcal H_q}\|
&\leq
2\exp\left(
-\frac{A_0^2(2\pi)^2|q|^2t}
{4\cdot10^{60}\kappa_iM^8}
\right)\\
&\leq
2\exp\left(
-\frac{R^{150}}{4\cdot10^{60}}
\right).
\end{aligned}
\tag{16}
\]

For every integer \(R\geq9\),

\[
\frac{R^{150}}{4\cdot10^{60}}\geq R.
\]

Therefore

\[
\boxed{
\|S_i(t)|_{\mathcal H_q}\|
\leq2e^{-R}
\leq R^{-1}
\leq\epsilon.
}
\tag{17}
\]

This also holds simultaneously for every supplied diffusivity.

The Fourier residue subspaces are orthogonal and invariant. Equations (14), (15) and (17) establish the required operator norm bound on every block of the mean-zero \(L^2\) space.
